question.problem:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(9,10)=0.8,\,F(9,4)=0.3,\,F(6,10)=0.4,\,F(6,4)=0.2,
$$

and the supports of $X$ and $Y$, respectively, are

$$
{S}_{X}=\{3,6,9,12\},\,{S}_{Y}=\{2,4,6,8,10,12\}.
$$

Find $P(6<X\le 9,4<Y\le 10).$
question.worked_solution:
Note the following:

- For a given joint PMF $f(x,y),$ we can think of each point where $f(x,y)\ne 0$ as a point mass in the plane, where the "probability mass" at each point equals the probability associated with that point.

- The joint CDF $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the total "probability mass" that lies in the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axis.

Given the supports of $X$ and $Y,$ the joint support $S$ is a subset of

$$
{S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}=\{3,6,9,12\}\times \{2,4,6,8,10,12\}.
$$

Let's sketch the points in ${S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y},$ which contains the joint support.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/7790a013e37bb86c00b44b1c022d6597f9bbdd57616c48e7ee7dfe8ddf512c63.png)

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/6535c5bf152e8a9b09bf5522cdc442668add6c4cc7a0df4e07307f9931886a80.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained as follows:

1\. Take the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(9,10).$

2\. Subtract the infinite rectangles that have their top-right corners at $(9,4)$ and $(6,10).$

3\. Finally, we need to add back the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(6,4).$ This is because we subtracted this region twice in step 2.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(6<X\le 9,4<Y\le 10) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(9,10)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 9,Y\le 10)}} \\  & \,-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(9,4)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 9,Y\le 4)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(6,10)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 6,Y\le 10)}} \\  & \,+\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(6,4)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 6,Y\le 4)}} \\  & =F(9,10)-F(9,4)-F(6,10)+F(6,4) \\  & =0.8-0.3-0.4+0.2 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$
